Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear success criteria and an actionable evaluation plan for the POC/trial.

Summary / success criteria
- Evaluate inference latency and cost for your 75-token average prompt with 2k-context and a concurrent 8-rps load. Target: p95 latency < 180ms and cost to be within the PO baseline we discussed.
- Validate integration: SSO via SAML, secure logs/audit access, and data retention controls.
- Functional: model quality pass on your 50-item prompt set (no more than 10% failure/regression rate vs baseline).
- Operational: deployment reproducibility and documented runbook for handoff to your infra team.

Proposed evaluation plan (3 weeks)
- Week 0 (Prep): exchange network & SSO artifacts, procurement PO number, and sign access terms.
- Week 1 (Env setup): spin up hosted sandbox (fastest) and optionally dedicated sandbox or VPC trial in parallel for comparison. Basic connectivity and demo runs.
- Week 2 (Workloads): run benchmark suite (latency/throughput), integrate SSO, and exercise evaluation prompts.
- Week 3 (Tuning & Handoff): tune batching/quantization suggestions, produce cost/perf report, and prepare handoff doc.

Ownership

- Redwood: Marissa (program owner), Chloe (customer success / account owner), Dev (technical lead for env setup & troubleshooting).

2) Acme: confirm whether you want us to prioritize a VPC trial (compliant) vs. running hosted sandbox first for faster results. We recommend hosted sandbox to start within 48-72 hours and spin up a VPC trial in parallel if you'd like comparison data.
3) Procurement: please share PO number or procurement ETA so we can schedule reserved sandbox if needed.

Hi all — quick technical note on environment tradeoffs and required artifacts so we can scope time to provision each option.

Hosted sandbox (fastest)
- Pros: no network setup from Acme side, can run end-to-end in ~48-72 hours, great for early quality checks and latency baselines.
- Cons: not appropriate for strict-compliance datasets / data residency requirements.

Dedicated sandbox (reserved host pool)
- Pros: isolated compute, predictable throughput, can be configured with tighter retention controls.
- Cons: provisioning lead-time (typically 3–5 business days if we need reserved capacity).

VPC trial (ACME-managed VPC peering / private network)
- Pros: meets highest compliance bar, traffic stays in your network, can map to your audit/KMS.
- Cons: needs network allowlist, cross-account IAM role or service-account approach, and potentially some infra coordination on your side (1–2 business days once artifacts are in place).

Required artifacts to start a VPC trial or dedicated sandbox:
- VPC CIDR + gateway/NAT info and any egress proxies
- List of allowed outbound endpoints (AWS region endpoints, ECR, etc.)
- SAML metadata (IdP cert + entity id) for SSO test
- Principal/service-account email to grant access (for dedicated) or an AWS role ARN (for VPC peering)
- Contact for your network engineer to coordinate a quick connectivity test

If you want the fastest path: we can provision a hosted sandbox in 48 hours. If you confirm VPC is required for compliance, we’ll do hosted as baseline and run VPC after we get the artifacts so you have comparative data.
